definition: The primary high-performance, pipelined system bus in the AMBA family, used for connecting CPUs, memory controllers, and DMA engines.
An open-standard, on-chip interconnect specification developed by ARM.
A simple, unpipelined AMBA bus used for low-bandwidth, low-power control registers.
The most advanced AMBA bus, featuring independent channels and out-of-order completion for high-speed multi-core SoCs.
A simplified version of AHB that removes multi-master arbitration and Split/Retry responses, designed to be used with a central Bus Matrix.
The latest AHB specification, adding support for TrustZone security (HNONSEC) and Exclusive Accesses (HEXCL).
The master clock for the AHB system. All signals are synchronous to its rising edge.
The active-low reset signal. Asserted asynchronously, de-asserted synchronously to HCLK.
The physical address requested by the master. Must be aligned to HSIZE.
Indicates direction. 1 = Write (master drives HWDATA), 0 = Read (slave drives HRDATA).
Specifies the privilege level and nature of the access (e.g., privileged vs user, cacheable vs non-cacheable).
The heartbeat of the bus. Driven by the master to indicate IDLE, BUSY, NONSEQ, or SEQ states.
The master does not require a data transfer. Slaves must respond with a zero-wait-state OKAY.
The master is continuing a burst but needs time to prepare the next beat. No data is transferred.
Non-Sequential. Indicates the first beat of a single transfer or a new burst.
Sequential. Indicates the next beat of an ongoing burst. The address is predictably related to the previous beat.
Specifies if the transfer is a SINGLE beat, or an INCR/WRAP burst of 4, 8, or 16 beats.
Specifies the byte size of each beat in the transfer (e.g., Byte, Halfword, Word).
Driven by the master during a write transfer.
Driven by the slave during a read transfer.
Driven by the slave to indicate the transfer is complete (1) or needs to wait (0).
The specific HREADY signal driven by a single slave before routing through the multiplexer to become the global HREADY.
Driven by the slave to indicate transfer success (OKAY) or failure (ERROR).
Indicates a locked transfer sequence that must not be interrupted by the arbiter.
Used in AHB5 to indicate an exclusive read or write (semaphore operation).
Driven by the slave in AHB5 to indicate if an exclusive write succeeded.
Used in AHB5 to indicate TrustZone security level (0 = Secure, 1 = Non-Secure).
A burst type where the address increments up to a specific boundary and then wraps back down to the start of the boundary.
The aligned address boundary within which a wrapping burst is confined. Calculated as (Number of beats) * (Bytes per beat).
A burst type where the address sequentially increments by the transfer size for every beat.
A standalone AHB transfer not part of any burst. Indicated by HBURST=SINGLE and HTRANS=NONSEQ.
The overlapping of the Address Phase of one transfer with the Data Phase of the previous transfer to achieve higher throughput.
The process by which an Arbiter decides which of multiple competing masters is granted access to the shared bus.
A non-blocking mechanism used by AHB5 (and AXI) to perform atomic read-modify-write operations, typically for semaphores, relying on an Exclusive Monitor rather than locking the bus.
A variable or hardware flag used to control access to a common resource in a concurrent system, often acquired via Exclusive Accesses.

A variation of a liveness property ('something good eventually happens') constrained to a specific time window. Used in hardware to prove responses occur within a realistic timeframe, rather than waiting indefinitely.
